records.source: תְּפִלָּה֮ לְמֹשֶׁ֪ה אִֽישׁ־הָאֱלֹ֫הִ֥יםאֲֽדֹנָ֗י מָע֣וֹן אַ֭תָּה הָיִ֥יתָ לָּ֗נוּ בְּדֹ֣ר וָדֹֽר׃
records.gloss: A prayer of Moses, [the] man of God. My Lord, a dwelling place you have been for us in generation and generation.
pieces: A prayer of Moses, the man of God. \q Lord, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have been our home through every generation.

L.1: A prayer of Moses, the man of God. \q My Lord, a dwelling place {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have been for us \q in generation and generation.

R.1: A prayer by Moses, the man of God. \q Lord, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have always been our home, \q from one generation to the next.

decisions.choice: The title shares verse 1
decisions.reason: This psalm's title is short and the Hebrew counts it together with the first line as verse 1, so here the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: Book Four of the Psalms begins
decisions.reason: The Psalms are gathered into five books. Book Three closed with the blessing of 89:53; Book Four (Psalms 90-106) opens here, and it closes with the blessing of 106:48.

decisions.choice: Moses, the man of God
decisions.reason: This is the only psalm with Moses' name in its title. "The man of God" is what Moses is called in Deuteronomy 33:1 and Joshua 14:6. The psalm echoes his words: God as a dwelling (Deuteronomy 33:27), humans returning to dust (Genesis 3:19), and the prayer "turn back" and "relent" (verse 13; Exodus 32:12).

decisions.choice: dwelling place: a home and a refuge
decisions.reason: The word (ma'on) is a dwelling, used of God's own home (26:8) and of an animal's den. Some Hebrew manuscripts and the ancient Greek translation read the similar word "refuge" (ma'oz); the sense is close.

decisions.choice: Lord
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable address God as "Lord" ('Adonai); Literal keeps "my Lord".

records.heading: Teach us to count our days

records.source: בְּטֶ֤רֶם׀הָ֘רִ֤ים יֻלָּ֗דוּ וַתְּח֣וֹלֵֽל אֶ֣רֶץ וְתֵבֵ֑ל וּֽמֵעוֹלָ֥ם עַד־ע֝וֹלָ֗ם אַתָּ֥ה אֵֽל׃
records.gloss: Before mountains were born and you brought forth [the] earth and [the] world, and from everlasting to everlasting you [are] God.
pieces: Before the mountains came to birth, \q before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} labored to bring to birth the earth and all the world, \q from the endless past to the endless future {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are God.

L.2: Before [the] mountains were born, \q and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought forth the earth and the world, \q even from everlasting to everlasting {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] God.

R.2: Before the mountains were made, \q before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought the earth and the world into being, \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} were God. You always have been, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} always will be.

decisions.choice: brought forth: gave birth with labor pains
alternatives: the earth was brought to birth
decisions.reason: The verb (chul) means to writhe in labor. Creation is pictured as a birth (Job 38:8-9; Proverbs 8:24-25). The form can also be read "and the earth was brought to birth", which the ancient Greek translation follows.

decisions.choice: from everlasting to everlasting: without beginning or end
decisions.reason: The word ('olam) reaches to the farthest time out of sight, behind and ahead. God ('El) was God before anything was made and will be after it.

decisions.choice: You always have been, and you always will be
alternatives: from everlasting to everlasting you are God
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "from everlasting to everlasting" means (m2).

records.source: תָּשֵׁ֣ב אֱ֭נוֹשׁ עַד־דַּכָּ֑א וַ֝תֹּ֗אמֶר שׁ֣וּבוּ בְנֵי־אָדָֽם׃
records.gloss: You turn humankind back to crushed [dust], and you said, Return, children of Adam.
pieces: You make mortals go back to dust; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} say, "Return, children of Adam."

L.3: You turn {{gender:mortals|man}} back to crushed [dust], \q and say, "Return, {{gender:children of Adam|sons of Adam}}."

R.3: You turn people back into dust. \q You say, "Go back, you humans."

decisions.choice: back to dust: the word to Adam
decisions.reason: The verse recalls Genesis 3:19, "to dust you will return", though the word here (dakka') means something crushed fine. "Children of Adam" (bene 'adam) means human beings, the descendants of the first man.

decisions.choice: Return: back to the dust
decisions.reason: The command most likely repeats the first half: God tells humans to go back to the dust. Some read it as a call to turn back to God, or as one generation going and the next coming.

decisions.choice: mortals, children of Adam (with "man", "sons of Adam" as the alternatives at Literal)
decisions.reason: The words mean any human being (8:5), so Literal gives inclusive wording by default with the traditional words as the alternative; Balanced and Readable use plurals.

records.source: כִּ֤י אֶ֪לֶף שָׁנִ֡ים בְּֽעֵינֶ֗יךָ כְּי֣וֹם אֶ֭תְמוֹל כִּ֣י יַעֲבֹ֑ר וְאַשְׁמוּרָ֥ה בַלָּֽיְלָה׃
records.gloss: For a thousand years in your eyes [are] like a day of yesterday when it passes, and a watch in the night.
pieces: For in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes a thousand years are like yesterday, once it has gone by, \q or like one watch of the night.

L.4: For a thousand years in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes \q [are] like yesterday's day when it passes, \q and [like] a watch in the night.

R.4: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, a thousand years are like one day that has already passed, \q or like a few hours of the night.

decisions.choice: a watch: one part of the night
decisions.reason: The night was divided into watches for guards, three in Israel (Judges 7:19; Lamentations 2:19). A watch passes in sleep and is gone.

decisions.choice: a thousand years like a day: 2 Peter 3:8
decisions.reason: 2 Peter 3:8 draws on this verse to say that God is not slow to keep his promise.

decisions.choice: a few hours of the night
decisions.reason: Readable says what a watch was (m1).

records.source: זְ֭רַמְתָּם שֵׁנָ֣ה יִהְי֑וּ בַּ֝בֹּ֗קֶר כֶּחָצִ֥יר יַחֲלֹֽף׃
records.gloss: You sweep them away; sleep they are; in the morning like grass [that] sprouts anew.
pieces: You wash them away like a flood. They are a passing sleep. \q When morning comes they are like grass that springs up again.

L.5: You sweep them away [as with a flood]; they are [like] sleep; \q in the morning [they are] like grass [that] sprouts anew.

R.5: You sweep people away as a flood does. Their life is as short as a night's sleep. \q They are like grass that comes up fresh in the morning.

decisions.choice: sweep away: carry off like a downpour
decisions.reason: The verb (zaram) is used of pouring rain (77:18). God carries humans off as a flood carries what is in its way.

decisions.choice: sleep: a brief sleep, or the sleep of death
decisions.reason: Life is like one night's sleep, over before it is noticed; sleep can also stand for death (13:4).

decisions.choice: in the morning: with the grass
decisions.reason: "In the morning" may close the first line (they are a sleep that ends in the morning) or open the second; verse 6 repeats it with the grass, so it is taken with the grass here.

decisions.choice: like a flood
decisions.reason: All three levels make the picture in the verb clear (m1); Literal brackets it.

records.source: בַּ֭בֹּקֶר יָצִ֣יץ וְחָלָ֑ף לָ֝עֶ֗רֶב יְמוֹלֵ֥ל וְיָבֵֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: In the morning it flourishes and sprouts anew; toward evening it withers and dries up.
pieces: In the morning it blooms and grows fresh; \q by evening it droops and dries out.

L.6: In the morning it flourishes and sprouts anew; \q by evening it withers and dries up.

R.6: In the morning it is green and growing. \q By evening it has wilted and dried up.

decisions.choice: grass that withers in a day
decisions.reason: In the land of Israel grass springs up after rain, and a hot wind can dry it out in a day. The Bible often uses it as a picture of how short human life is (103:15-16; Isaiah 40:6-8).

records.gloss: For we come to an end in your anger, and by your fury we are terrified.
pieces: For we are worn away by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger \q and struck with terror by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} rage.

L.7: For we come to an end in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger, \q and by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} fury we are terrified.

R.7: Your anger is destroying us. \q Your fury fills us with fear.

decisions.choice: death and God's anger
decisions.reason: The psalm links the shortness of life to God's anger at sin (verse 8), as when the generation that came out of Egypt died in the wilderness (Numbers 14:29-35).

decisions.choice: terrified: thrown into panic
decisions.reason: The verb (bahal) means to be shaken with alarm (6:3-4).

records.source: שַׁתָּ֣ה עֲוֺנֹתֵ֣ינוּ לְנֶגְדֶּ֑ךָ עֲ֝לֻמֵ֗נוּ לִמְא֥וֹר פָּנֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: You have set our iniquities before you, our hidden [sins] in [the] light of your face.
pieces: You have laid our wrongs out before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q what we hid is lit up by the light of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face.

L.8: You have set our iniquities before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q our hidden [sins] in the light of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face.

R.8: You see all our sins. \q Even the sins we have hidden are as clear to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} as things in bright light.

decisions.choice: you have set: the word as read, not as written
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew text writes the verb without its final letter and its notes say to read the full form. The meaning is the same. The words follow the form to be read.

decisions.choice: our hidden things: sins kept secret
decisions.reason: The word ('alumim) means what is hidden, here the sins no one else sees (19:13). A word spelled the same way means youth, and so some read "the sins of our youth".

decisions.choice: the light of your face: God's sight
decisions.reason: Elsewhere the light of God's face is his favor (4:7; 89:16); here nothing can hide from it.

records.source: כִּ֣י כָל־יָ֭מֵינוּ פָּנ֣וּ בְעֶבְרָתֶ֑ךָ כִּלִּ֖ינוּ שָׁנֵ֣ינוּ כְמוֹ־הֶֽגֶה׃
records.gloss: For all our days turn away in your fury; we finish our years like a sigh.
pieces: All our days slip away under {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wrath; \q our years end like a sigh.

L.9: For all our days turn away in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} fury; \q we finish our years like a sigh.

R.9: Because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are angry, our days slip away. \q Our years end as quickly as a breath.

decisions.choice: a sigh: a murmur that is soon gone
decisions.reason: The word (hegeh) is a low sound, a sigh or a groan (Ezekiel 2:10). The older sense "a tale" comes from the related verb "to murmur, to ponder".

decisions.choice: turn away: pass, decline
decisions.reason: The days "turn" like the day turning toward evening (Jeremiah 6:4): they decline and are gone.

records.source: יְמֵֽי־שְׁנוֹתֵ֨ינוּ בָהֶ֥ם שִׁבְעִ֪ים שָׁנָ֡ה וְאִ֤ם בִּגְבוּרֹ֨ת׀שְׁמ֘וֹנִ֤ים שָׁנָ֗ה וְ֭רָהְבָּם עָמָ֣ל וָאָ֑וֶן כִּי־גָ֥ז חִ֝֗ישׁ וַנָּעֻֽפָה׃
records.gloss: The days of our years — in them [are] seventy years, or if with strength, eighty years; and their pride [is] toil and trouble, for it passes quickly, and we fly away.
pieces: Our lifetime lasts seventy years, or eighty for the strong; \q yet even its best is toil and sorrow, \q for it hurries past, and we take flight.

L.10: The days of our years — in them [are] seventy years, or if [there is] strength, eighty years; \q and their pride [is] toil and trouble, \q for it passes quickly, and we fly away.

R.10: We live seventy years, or maybe eighty if we have the strength. \q But even our best years are full of hard work and trouble. \q They pass quickly, and then we are gone.

decisions.choice: their pride: the best of them
decisions.reason: The word (rohav) means pride or boasting: what people are proud of in their years, their best, is still toil. The ancient Greek translation reads a word meaning "most of them".

decisions.choice: toil and trouble: hard work and sorrow
decisions.reason: The first word ('amal) is wearying labor; the second ('awen) is trouble or mischief, here hardship (Genesis 35:18 names a son "son of my sorrow" with it).

decisions.choice: we fly away: we die
decisions.reason: Life passes like a bird taking flight; the psalm does not say where.

records.gloss: Who knows [the] strength of your anger, and like your fear, your fury?
pieces: Who knows the force of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger? \q Your fury matches the reverence {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} deserve.

L.11: Who knows the strength of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger, \q and [who knows] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} fury [that is] like the fear [due] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?

R.11: No one truly knows how strong {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger is. \q Your anger is as great as the fear and respect {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} deserve.

decisions.choice: like your fear, your fury: your wrath is as great as the awe due to you
alternatives: who knows your fury as your fear deserves?
decisions.reason: The short line can mean that God's wrath is as great as the fear that is rightly his, or that no one fears him as much as his wrath should make them. The first is followed.

decisions.choice: your fear: the awe and reverence due to God
decisions.reason: "Your fear" here is the fear people owe to God, not fear that God feels (2:11; 5:8).

records.source: לִמְנ֣וֹת יָ֭מֵינוּ כֵּ֣ן הוֹדַ֑ע וְ֝נָבִ֗א לְבַ֣ב חָכְמָֽה׃
records.gloss: To count our days so teach [us], that we may bring [in] a heart of wisdom.
pieces: Teach us, then, to reckon our days rightly, \q so that our hearts may grow wise.

L.12: So teach [us] to count our days, \q that we may bring [in] a heart of wisdom.

R.12: Teach us to understand how short our life is, \q so that we will live wisely.

decisions.choice: count our days: grasp how few they are
decisions.reason: To count the days is to take the measure of life and see how short it is (39:5).

decisions.choice: bring a heart of wisdom: gain a wise heart
alternatives: bring in a harvest of wisdom
decisions.reason: The verb (bo', causative) means to bring in, perhaps as a harvest is brought in. The heart is the mind and will, so a wise heart is a life guided by wisdom.

decisions.choice: how short our life is; live wisely
decisions.reason: Readable says what counting the days means and what a wise heart is (m1, m2).

records.gloss: Return, YHWH! Until when? And have compassion on your servants.
pieces: Turn back to us, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}! How long must we wait? \q Show pity to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants.

L.13: Return, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}! Until when? \q And have compassion on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants.

R.13: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, come back to us! How long will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} stay away? \q Be kind to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants.

decisions.choice: Return and relent: the prayer of Moses
decisions.reason: Moses prayed with the same two verbs after the golden calf: "turn from your burning anger and relent" (Exodus 32:12). The psalm asks God to turn from his anger toward his people again.

decisions.choice: have compassion: relent, change course in pity
decisions.reason: The verb (nicham) means to be moved to pity, and so to turn from a course of action (Exodus 32:14).

decisions.choice: Turn back to us (B); come back to us (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say to whom God is asked to return.

records.source: שַׂבְּעֵ֣נוּ בַבֹּ֣קֶר חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ וּֽנְרַנְּנָ֥ה וְ֝נִשְׂמְחָ֗ה בְּכָל־יָמֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: Satisfy us in the morning [with] your loyal love, that we may shout for joy and rejoice in all our days.
pieces: Fill us with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love at daybreak, \q and we will shout for joy and rejoice as long as we live.

L.14: Satisfy us in the morning [with] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love, \q that we may shout for joy and rejoice in all our days.

R.14: Each morning, fill our lives with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful love. \q Then we will sing for joy and be happy all our lives.

decisions.choice: loyal love: chesed
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith, God's commitment to his people that does not give up (5:8).

decisions.choice: in the morning: after the night is over
decisions.reason: Morning is the time when help comes after a night of trouble (30:6; 46:6), and it answers the grass that withers by evening (verse 6).

decisions.choice: faithful love
decisions.reason: As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

records.source: שַׂ֭מְּחֵנוּ כִּימ֣וֹת עִנִּיתָ֑נוּ שְׁ֝נ֗וֹת רָאִ֥ינוּ רָעָֽה׃
records.gloss: Make us glad according to [the] days you afflicted us, [the] years we saw evil.
pieces: Match the days {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought us low with days of gladness, \q and the years of hardship we have known with years of joy.

L.15: Make us glad according to the days {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} afflicted us, \q the years we have seen evil.

R.15: Make us happy for as long as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made us suffer. \q Give us good years to make up for the bad years we have lived through.

decisions.choice: evil: harm, hardship
decisions.reason: The word (ra'ah) here is evil that happens to people, trouble, not wrong that they do.

decisions.choice: according to the days: as many as the days
decisions.reason: The prayer asks for joy in the same measure as the suffering: as many glad days as there were days of affliction.

decisions.choice: days of gladness, years of joy (B); good years (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out the comparison (m2).

records.gloss: Let your work appear to your servants, and your majesty upon their children.
pieces: Let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants see {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} deeds, \q and let their children see {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} splendor.

L.16: Let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} work appear to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants, \q and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} majesty upon their children.

R.16: Let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants see the great things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do. \q Let their children see how glorious {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are.

decisions.choice: your work: God's saving acts
decisions.reason: The word (po'al) is used of what God has done for his people (44:2; 77:13).

decisions.choice: their children: the next generation
decisions.reason: The generation that died in the wilderness did not see the land, but their children did (Numbers 14:31). The prayer asks that God's deeds be seen by those who come after.

records.source: וִיהִ֤י׀נֹ֤עַם אֲדֹנָ֥י אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ עָ֫לֵ֥ינוּ וּמַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יָ֭דֵינוּ כּוֹנְנָ֥ה עָלֵ֑ינוּ וּֽמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָ֝דֵ֗ינוּ כּוֹנְנֵֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And let the kindness of [the] Lord our God be upon us, and the work of our hands establish for us; and the work of our hands, establish it.
pieces: May the Lord our God show us {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kindness. \q Give lasting worth to the work of our hands; \q yes, give the work of our hands lasting worth.

L.17: And let the kindness of the Lord our God be upon us, \q and the work of our hands establish for us; \q yes, the work of our hands, establish it.

R.17: May the Lord our God be good to us. \q Make the work we do succeed and last. \q Yes, make our work last!

decisions.choice: kindness: pleasantness, favor
decisions.reason: The word (no'am) means what is pleasant and lovely (27:4). Here it is God's goodness resting on his people.

decisions.choice: establish: make firm and lasting
decisions.reason: The verb (kun) means to set firm. Human life is short (verses 3-10); the prayer asks that what people do will not be lost.

decisions.choice: the repeated request
decisions.reason: The last line repeats the request for emphasis and closes the psalm.

decisions.choice: show us his kindness (B); be good to us (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what it means for God's kindness to be on his people.
